name: Question 1
problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}={x}^{2}+2y,\,y(0)=0
$$

Using the implicit Euler method with step size $Δx=0.5,$ the new value ${y}_{\text{new}}$ is obtained by solving the equation $g({y}_{\text{new}})=0$ at each step.
Which of the following is the **general form** of $g({y}_{\text{new}})$ in terms of the new values ${x}_{\text{new}}$ and ${y}_{\text{new}},$ and the current value $y?$
worked_solution:
For an initial value problem

$$
{y}^{′}=f(x,y),\,{y}_{0}=y({x}_{0}),
$$

the implicit Euler method with step size $Δx$ is given by

$$
Δy={y}_{\text{new}}^{′}\cdot Δx,
$$

with ${y}_{\text{new}}^{′}=f({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{\text{new}})$ evaluated at the next $x$ and $y$ values.

In general $Δy$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & ={y}_{\text{new}}^{′}\cdot Δx \\  & =(({x}_{\text{new}})^{2}+2{y}_{\text{new}})\cdot 0.5 \\  & =0.5({x}_{\text{new}})^{2}+{y}_{\text{new}}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute this into ${y}_{\text{new}}=y+Δy$ and move all terms to the left-hand side to define $g({y}_{\text{new}}):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+0.5({x}_{\text{new}})^{2}+{y}_{\text{new}} \\ {{{y}_{\text{new}}-y-0.5({x}_{\text{new}})^{2}-{y}_{\text{new}}}_{⏟}}_{g({y}_{\text{new}})} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general form of the function $g$ for step size $Δx=0.5$ is

$$
g({y}_{\text{new}})=-\,y-0.5({x}_{\text{new}})^{2}.
$$

Question 1
?

Consider the following initial value problem: y′=x2+2y,y(0)=0 Using the implicit Euler method with step size Δx=0.5, the new value ynew is obtained by solving the equation g(ynew)=0 at each step. Which of the following is the general form of g(ynew) in terms of the new values xnew and ynew, and the current value y?

a
g(ynew)=−ynew+y−0.5(xnew)2
b
g(ynew)=ynew−y−ynew−0.5(xnew)2
c
g(ynew)=ynew−y−0.5(xnew)2
d
g(ynew)=−y−0.5(xnew)2
e
g(ynew)=−y−0.5y2
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

For an initial value problem y′=f(x,y),y0=y(x0), the implicit Euler method with step size Δx is given by Δy=ynew′⋅Δx, with ynew′=f(xnew,ynew) evaluated at the next x and y values.

In general Δy is given by

Δy=ynew′⋅Δx=((xnew)2+2ynew)⋅0.5=0.5(xnew)2+ynew.

We substitute this into ynew=y+Δy and move all terms to the left-hand side to define g(ynew):

ynew=y+Δyynew=y+0.5(xnew)2+ynewynew−y−0.5(xnew)2−ynew⏟g(ynew)=0.

Therefore, the general form of the function g for step size Δx=0.5 is g(ynew)=−y−0.5(xnew)2.
